name: Tax preparer

google_prefill.phone: [G] the listed phone (stays the business's; customers use Rosie's one number)

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)

services.name: Simple return
services.story: The main story: a $35 simple return with Kevin. Nothing is taken, and a YES books it. Alex pays at the front desk when the return is ready to sign, before Kevin files it.

services.name: Simple return
services.story: The same $35 return on a Saturday morning, when Kevin works alone with no front desk, or by video: Rosie texts the bill when Kevin texts DONE. It's paid before the return is filed.

services.name: Prior-year return
services.story: A prior-year return, quoted from the papers Alex uploads first: Kevin quotes $90, and Sam OKs it. Nothing is taken; it's paid at the front desk before filing.

services.name: Amended return
services.story: An amended return, priced at the sit-down once Kevin sees the papers. Only the $25 review fee is promised, and it's paid at the front desk.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer

services.name: Home tax return
services.story: The main story: a $179 return at Alex's home. Nothing is taken. Rosie texts the bill when Daniel texts DONE, and it's paid before he files.

services.name: Home tax return
services.story: The same $179 return, paid the office's own way: its own invoice, or, where the office offers it, the fee taken from the refund through its bank partner.

services.name: Several late years
services.story: Several late years, quoted at $640 from the papers Alex uploads first. Over $500, so Sam OKs it. Nothing is taken; Rosie texts the bill after.

questions_before_times: Which tax year or years, and is the return late?
Which kinds of forms do you have: just W-2s, or 1099s, a side business, rentals or stock sales? Only the kinds, never amounts. This sets the price and the length.
A sit-down at the office, by video or phone, or a drop-off?
A visit at your place: a home, a care home, or a host's tax day?
license: Each paid preparer: a federal preparer ID number (a PTIN), renewed every year. A credential where they hold one: an enrolled agent, a CPA or an attorney. The office: a business registration.
